# brig sync

Apply a VM's OpenShell config directories to its gateway

## Synopsis

```text
brig sync [NAME]
```

## Description

Apply a VM's OpenShell config directories to its gateway. [`brig start`](brig-start.md) does
the same every time the VM starts.

A config directory may hold:

```text
profiles/*.yaml        OpenShell provider profiles, imported into the
                       gateway's default workspace or updated there
providers/*.yaml       providers whose credentials brig reads from your
                       keyring with secret-tool, for example:
                         name: github
                         type: github
                         credentials:
                           GH_TOKEN:
                             secret_tool:
                               lookup: [service, github.com, user, alice]
                       or, where there is no keyring, a credential
                       read from an environment variable of brig's own:
                           GH_TOKEN:
                             env: BRIG_SECRET_GH_TOKEN
workspaces/WS/profiles/*.yaml, workspaces/WS/providers/*.yaml
                       the same for the workspace WS, which brig
                       creates on the gateway if it is missing
policies/default.yaml  the default policy for new sandboxes, which
                       brig use NAME and eval "$(brig env NAME)"
                       export as OPENSHELL_SANDBOX_POLICY
services/*.yaml        the secrets of a service (see brig service
                       --help), in a config directory of its VM:
                         name: mirror
                         secrets:
                           UPSTREAM_TOKEN:
                             secret_tool:
                               lookup: [service, mirror.example.org]
```

Every workspace is synced on its own: the default workspace first, then
the others by name, with a "workspace WS:" heading each when there is more
than one. The same profile ID or provider name may appear in several
workspaces; they are separate objects. --workspace WS (repeatable) syncs
only the named workspaces, by default the one that $BRIG\_WORKSPACE names
if it is set. --prune deletes only what brig created in the
workspace it is synced for, and brig never deletes a workspace itself.
policies/ is not per workspace.

Secrets never appear in config directories, on command lines or on the
host's disk (the gateway keeps them encrypted on the VM's data disk): brig
runs "secret-tool lookup application brig ATTRIBUTE VALUE..." (or the
program set as openshell.secret\_tool in config.yaml) or reads the
BRIG\_SECRET\_\* variable that a credential names, and hands the value to the openshell CLI in its
environment. A provider is updated only when one of its
secrets changed. Profiles and providers that brig did not create are
only touched when a config directory defines them, and never deleted.

A provider's credentials may be sent to the endpoints of its profile.
[`brig start`](brig-start.md) keeps back a change of a profile whose credentials the gateway
holds already, unless it changes only the profile's name, description or
category: credentials, endpoints, rules and binaries decide where and how
the credentials are sent. Once the gateway holds credentials that brig
set, [`brig start`](brig-start.md) also keeps back new providers, providers that brig did not
create, and credentials that a provider file now looks up elsewhere, since
each could send a secret to other endpoints. brig sync applies them and
says what it changes. Check shared profiles with --dry-run first.

For a gateway VM, brig sync and every start also bring its services in
line: the relays and profiles of the services that its sandboxes are
attached to, a new token for a sandbox whose provider is gone, and no token
for a sandbox that is gone. For a service VM, brig sync hands the service
its secrets again and restarts it.

## Examples

```sh
brig sync dev --dry-run
brig sync dev --prune
brig sync dev --workspace team
```

## Options

| Option | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | show what would change, without changing it |
| `-o, --output format` | output format: table or json (default `table`) |
| `--prune` | delete profiles and providers that brig created but no config directory defines any more |
| `--refresh-secrets` | update every provider's credentials, whether or not they changed |
| `--secret-tool string` | program to look secrets up with (default: openshell.secret\_tool from config.yaml) |
| `-w, --workspace stringArray` | sync only this workspace (repeatable; default: $BRIG\_WORKSPACE, else every workspace the config directories define) |

The [global options](brig.md#options) of brig apply too.
